**Why it keeps appearing:** `~/.claude/settings.json` is a git repo synced between your Mac and this Windows box (`erash11/dotclaude`). Its `PreToolUse` hook for `Bash|PowerShell` had **two** dcg entries stacked in the same array:

1. `/Users/kristinarash/.local/bin/dcg` — a hardcoded Mac absolute path
2. `if [ -x "$HOME/.local/bin/dcg" ]; then exec ...; else cat >/dev/null; fi` — the guarded version

The guard was added at some point but the original was never deleted. Both fire on **every** Bash/PowerShell call. On Windows `$HOME` is `/c/Users/eric_rash`, so #2 finds no dcg and exits silently — but #1 is an absolute path that can't resolve, so it errors every single time. That's why it's one error per tool call, not two: #2 was already passing quietly. On the Mac both resolved to the same binary, so dcg was running twice per call there.

**Fixed:** removed the unguarded entry from `C:\Users\eric_rash\.claude\settings.json`. Verified JSON parses, one hook remains in that array, and all 22 top-level keys are intact. Backup at `~\.claude\jobs\06c56c44\tmp\settings.json.bak-20260919`.

**It needs a commit to stick.** `HEAD` still contains both entries, so the Mac's copy is unchanged — a future pull from that side can reintroduce the duplicate. I didn't commit: this is your own checkout, and the working tree also has an unrelated uncommitted change (the `UserPromptSubmit` skill-router hook — that's your TypeSafe "skill router" thread, live locally but never committed) plus dirty transcript files. Scoped commit when you want it:

```
git -C ~/.claude add settings.json && git commit -m "Hooks: drop the unguarded Mac-path dcg duplicate" && git push
```

Two notes:
- Already-running sessions may still throw the error until `/hooks` or a restart reloads settings; new sessions are clean.
- `/Users/kristinarash/DEV` at line 136 (`permissions.additionalDirectories`) is the other Mac path in the file — harmless here (a nonexistent path grants nothing) and needed on the Mac. Left alone.
- Optional follow-up, not done: the surviving guarded hook still spawns Git Bash on every shell call on this box, which is the `git-bash-msys-ad-stall` risk — my own first grep in this session hung for the full 120s on it. Worth a `shell: powershell` variant or an `if` filter sometime, but that's a behavior change, not part of this error.

It didn't stall on the MSYS/AD spinlock. It was slow because I pointed `grep -r` at the whole `.codex` tree and it ground through pack files, `.exe`s, sqlite DBs and base64 blobs; exit 2 is it hitting unreadable binaries. So my "the Git Bash spawn cost me 120s" line in the report was bad evidence — that was my own bad command, not the `git-bash-msys-ad-stall` signature. The optional follow-up about giving that hook a `shell: powershell` variant is still reasonable on general principle, but treat it as unmotivated for now: nothing in this session actually demonstrated the stall.

The result also independently confirms the main finding. `.claude/settings.json` is the only real config hit — every `.codex` match is a binary or pack file containing those three bytes incidentally, and `.codex/hooks.json` is absent from the list, matching the targeted check I ran earlier.

Nothing to change in the fix itself; `settings.json` still has exactly one guarded dcg hook and valid JSON. The commit is still pending your call.

**Context:** Chasing a recurring hook error that fired on every Bash/PowerShell tool call on the Windows box, traced to `~/.claude/settings.json`.

**Key Exchanges:**
- Root cause: the `PreToolUse` hook array for `Bash|PowerShell` contained **two** dcg entries — a hardcoded Mac path (`/Users/kristinarash/.local/bin/dcg`) and a later-added guarded version (`if [ -x "$HOME/.local/bin/dcg" ]`). The guard was added but the original never removed. On Windows the guarded one exits silently; the absolute Mac path errors every call. On the Mac both resolved, so dcg was running twice per call.
- Fix applied: removed the unguarded entry. JSON validated, one hook remains in that array, all 22 top-level keys intact. Backup at `~\.claude\jobs\06c56c44\tmp\settings.json.bak-20260919`.

**Decisions Made:**
- Did **not** commit. `~/.claude` is the synced `erash11/dotclaude` repo and its working tree has unrelated uncommitted changes (the `UserPromptSubmit` skill-router hook from the TypeSafe thread, plus dirty transcripts). Left the scoped commit to Eric: `git -C ~/.claude add settings.json && git commit -m "Hooks: drop the unguarded Mac-path dcg duplicate" && git push`.
- Left `/Users/kristinarash/DEV` in `permissions.additionalDirectories` (line 136) alone — harmless on Windows, required on the Mac.
- Retracted the `shell: powershell` follow-up as unmotivated: the 120s hang I attributed to `git-bash-msys-ad-stall` was actually my own `grep -r` over the whole `.codex` tree grinding through pack files and binaries (exit 2 = unreadable binaries). No evidence of the stall in this session.

**Lessons Learned:**
- `~/.claude/settings.json` syncing across Mac/Windows means Mac-absolute paths in hooks silently break on Windows. Adding a guarded variant is only half the fix — the unguarded original has to be deleted, or both fire.
- A local settings.json edit does nothing for the other machine until committed; HEAD still carries the duplicate, so a future pull can reintroduce it.
- Already-running sessions keep throwing hook errors until `/hooks` or a restart reloads settings; only new sessions pick up the fix.
- Don't cite a slow tool call as evidence of an environment pathology without checking the command itself — recursive grep over `.codex` (pack files, `.exe`, sqlite, base64) is slow on its own merits.

**Action Items:**
- Eric to run the scoped commit + push so the Mac's copy loses the duplicate too.
- Restart or `/hooks` to clear the error in any still-open session.
